meta.documentTitle: Mahabharat Episode 2: The Origin of the Chandravamshis

header.title: Mahabharat Episode 2: The Origin of the Chandravamshis
header.description: The complete story of King Sudhyumna's transformation, the birth of the lunar dynasty, Emperor Nahusha's fall, and Kacha's quest for the secret Sanjeevini mantra.

intro.title: Understanding the Lunar Lineage
leads: To truly understand the grand story of the Mahabharat, we must look closely at the royal dynasties that shaped this ancient world.
Unlike the firm, black-and-white Sun Dynasty (Suryavamshis), the Moon Dynasty (Chandravamshis) is driven by intense emotions, art, dramatic changes, and deeply human flaws.
This episode reveals how the Chandravamshi line was born and why its kings often acted out of intense emotional flare-ups.

storyElements.html: One day, King Sudhyumna went hunting in a forest where Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati were living.
Looking at the wild male animals, Parvati said to Shiva that their presence felt like an insult to his supreme manhood.

bubble.text: I want you to make this forest in such a way that there is no other male here but you.

storyElements.html: Shiva was in a romantic mood and agreed. Instantly, everything in the forest turned female.
Bull elephants became cow elephants, male lions became lionesses, peacocks became peahens, and King Sudhyumna suddenly turned into a woman!
Shocked and confused, the king searched the forest to find out who had done this to him.
When he found Shiva and Parvati, he fell at Shiva's feet and begged for help.

bubble.text: This is not fair! I am a king, a man, and I have a family. I just came to hunt. How can I go back home like this?
I cannot take back what I have done, but I can correct it a bit. When the moon is waning, you will be a woman. When the moon is waxing, you will be a man.

storyElements.html: King Sudhyumna was ashamed to go back to his kingdom. He stayed in the forest and became known as Ela.
Ela lived as a man for half the month and as a woman for the other half.
One day, Ela met Budha (the child of Chandra and Tara). Budha was also neither fully a man nor fully a woman because of Brihaspati's curse.
It was a perfect match, as both were male and female in equal measure. They had many children together, and these children became the first Chandravamshis (descendants of the Moon).
In ancient Indian history, there were two main lines of kings: Suryavamshis (Sun line) and Chandravamshis (Moon line).
Suryavamshis were clear-cut, direct, and conquerors like Manu, Ikshvaku, Rama, and Harishchandra.
Chandravamshis changed like the moon every day—they were emotional, artistic, dynamic, and unpredictable. The Kurus of the Mahabharat belong to this emotional Chandravamshi line.
One of Budha and Ela's children was Nahusha, who became a powerful emperor on Earth.
Once, Indra had to leave his kingdom, Devaloka. He invited Nahusha to temporarily sit on the throne and rule in his place.
Nahusha became extremely proud of this power. He started calling celestial nymphs (apsaras) and then demanded Indra's wife, Shachi.

bubble.text: Now I am sitting on Indra's throne. I am Indra now. You belong to me!
If you want me, you must come to my palace on a palanquin carried by the Sapta Rishis (the seven great sages).

storyElements.html: Nahusha foolishly ordered the holy sages to carry his palanquin.
In his rush and pride, he felt the sages were walking too slowly. He kicked sage Agastya Muni on the head and shouted, "Go faster!"

bubble.text: Pride has gone to your head! You are unfit to live in heaven or even be human. Fall down and become a python!

storyElements.html: Nahusha instantly fell from heaven to Earth as a giant python.
Nahusha had two main sons: Yati, who saw the world's vanity and became a peaceful monk in the Himalayas, and Yayati, who became the next king.
During this time, the Devas (gods) and Asuras (demons) were fighting continuous battles for control of fertile lands.
Brihaspati was the priest of the Devas, and Shukracharya was the priest of the Asuras.
The Asuras had a huge advantage: Shukracharya possessed the secret Sanjeevini mantra, which could bring dead people back to life.
At the end of every battle day, Shukracharya revived all the killed Asuras. By next morning, they were ready to fight again!
Desperate to solve this problem, Brihaspati sent his son, Kacha, to learn the secret mantra from Shukracharya.
Kacha went to Shukracharya's gurukul, bowed down, and requested to be taught.

bubble.text: I am Kacha, son of Brihaspati. I come from a good family. Please accept me as your student.

storyElements.html: The Asuras warned Shukracharya that Kacha was a spy sent to steal the Sanjeevini secret.
However, Shukracharya followed the rules of dharma: if a qualified student asks for knowledge, a teacher cannot reject him.
Kacha served his teacher faithfully. Shukracharya's daughter, Devyani, fell deeply in love with Kacha, but Kacha stayed completely focused on his mission.
The Asuras were determined to get rid of Kacha.
First attack: While Kacha was grazing cattle in the forest, the Asuras killed him, tore his body into pieces, and fed him to wild animals.
When only cows returned home, Devyani cried to her father. Shukracharya used Sanjeevini to bring Kacha back to life.
Second attack: A few days later, while Kacha was plucking flowers, the Asuras caught him again.
This time, they ground his body into paste, mixed it with ocean water, and put a part of his ground organs into Shukracharya's wine!
Unknowingly, Shukracharya drank the wine containing Kacha.

bubble.text: Kacha is missing again! Bring him back, father, or I will drown myself in the lake!

storyElements.html: Shukracharya chanted the mantra, but felt a strange rumbling in his own stomach.
From inside his belly, Kacha spoke up and explained how the Asuras had trickily fed him to Shukracharya.
Shukracharya was trapped in a terrible dilemma:
If Kacha stays inside, he dies. If Kacha comes out, he will tear open Shukracharya's stomach and Shukracharya will die.

bubble.text: Kacha, you are worthy. I will teach you the Sanjeevini mantra right now while you are in my stomach. Then burst out of me, and immediately use the mantra to bring me back to life!

storyElements.html: Kacha memorized the secret mantra. He burst out of Shukracharya's body, which instantly killed the teacher.
Kacha then quickly recited the Sanjeevini mantra and revived Shukracharya back to life. His mission was complete!

bubble.text: Now that everything is fine, marry me! I have loved you for so long.
I cannot marry you. You are my teacher's daughter, which makes you like a sister. Also, since I came out of your father's body, he is like my mother, making you my sister twice over.

storyElements.html: Despite Devyani's crying and pleading, Kacha stood firm on his duty and walked away back to heaven with the secret knowledge.
